overview: The CONNECT Act rewrites the goals of the John H. Chafee program, which funds state services for young people transitioning out of foster care, to put lasting relationships first. The program's purposes would include helping youth who were in foster care at age 14 or older build and keep supportive ties with adults, relatives, family friends, mentors and peers. It would also support youth still in foster care in taking part in planning their own long-term living arrangements and connect them with peer support, mentoring and other services. Within a year, the Department of Health and Human Services must issue guidance to states and tribes, developed with input from former foster youth, on eligible services, best practices for mentoring and peer support, outreach, and recordkeeping. As of May 11, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say having caring adults and peers to rely on is one of the strongest supports a young person leaving foster care can have, and the program's goals should reflect that.
against: Critics say updating a program's stated purposes and issuing guidance does not by itself add services or funding, so the practical effect may be limited.
